maintenance_led_reason: Mostly sells new heat tracing, heaters and boilers for capital projects; maintenance and retrofit is a smaller share.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are private oil and gas, chemical, power and industrial firms buying heat tracing and heaters.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly organically through engineered heating products; only occasional acquisitions, such as boilers and data-center thermal deals.
mission_critical_reason: Engineered heat tracing and freeze protection are specified into plants; hazardous-location certification and process safety make switching costly.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes from claims adjusting and third-party administration services for insurers and self-insured clients, not repairing or maintaining installed equipment.
publicly_funded_reason: Clients are mainly private insurers and corporations paying for claims handling and TPA services, not government.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly through its own claims services; past acquisitions like Broadspire and GAB Robins were occasional large deals.
mission_critical_reason: Outsourced claims handling and TPA services are embedded in insurers' operations and regulated, so switching brings disruption and risk.

maintenance_led_reason: Sells subscription CXM software (Service, Social, Insights, Marketing suites) to enterprises, not repair, servicing or replacement of installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are private global brands like Microsoft, Uber, Shell, 3M and Dow paying for software subscriptions.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly by selling its own unified AI-native platform on a single codebase; no sign of roll-up acquisitions.
mission_critical_reason: Enterprise platform unifying customer service, social and insights across 30+ channels; switching means migration, retraining and integration disruption.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes from carriers paying for consumer leads and customer acquisition in auto and home insurance, not repair or servicing.
publicly_funded_reason: Paying customers are private insurance carriers and agents; consumers use the quote service free.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows organically through its online insurance marketplace and AI matching; acquisitions are only occasional.
mission_critical_reason: Carriers buy leads and referrals from many sources and can shift marketing spend easily; no integration lock-in.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes from franchise royalties and company-operated restaurant sales of burgers and food, which are consumables, not repairs or servicing.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are consumers buying fast-food burgers; franchisees pay royalties. No government payer.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly by franchising and opening restaurants and menu sales, not through a steady stream of acquisitions.
mission_critical_reason: Consumers can easily switch to other fast-food restaurants. Franchisees are tied by contracts, but the end customer buys on choice.
notes: Franchisees face switching costs, but the answer reflects the consumer-facing burger business.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue is mainly hotel room, food and beverage income from guests at 29 owned hotels, not repair or replacement work.
publicly_funded_reason: Paid by leisure and business travelers and groups staying at its Hilton, Marriott and Hyatt-branded hotels and resorts.
serial_acquirer_reason: Lodging REIT with 29 hotels that recycles capital and sells assets; growth is not from a steady stream of acquisitions.
mission_critical_reason: Hotel guests and groups can easily choose other hotels; no switching cost for travelers.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue is recurring SaaS subscriptions for payroll and HCM software sold to employers, not repair, servicing or replacement of installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are private businesses, franchises and associations paying for payroll and HR software; government is not the final payer.
serial_acquirer_reason: Growth is mainly organic through selling its HCM platform; Airbase was a notable deal, but acquisitions are occasional.
mission_critical_reason: Core payroll, tax filing and HR platform; switching means data migration, retraining and payroll accuracy and compliance risk.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes from auction fees and services on salvage and used vehicle sales, not repairing or servicing installed equipment.
publicly_funded_reason: Sellers are insurers, fleets and dealers; buyers are dealers, rebuilders and consumers, all privately paid.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly by organic volume, new yards and international expansion, with only occasional yard or business acquisitions.
mission_critical_reason: Insurers rely on Copart's integrated salvage logistics, yard network and online auction platform; switching disrupts claims processing and recovery.
notes: Mission-critical judgment is moderate; buyers can switch auctions easily, but insurer sellers face higher switching costs.

maintenance_led_reason: Sells Suboxone film and Sublocade injection for opioid use disorder; prescription drugs, not repair or servicing of installed assets.
publicly_funded_reason: Sublocade and Suboxone are largely paid by Medicaid and Medicare in the US, though commercial insurers also pay.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows by selling its own OUD products such as Sublocade and Suboxone and by developing new ones, not by regular acquisitions.
mission_critical_reason: Patients stabilised on Sublocade or Suboxone face clinical risk of relapse if switched; branded, regulated, prescriber-managed treatment.
notes: Medicaid share of revenue is from general knowledge, not from the website text, so the funding answer is less certain.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes from recruiter job-posting and resume-database subscriptions on Dice and ClearanceJobs, not repair or servicing of installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Paid by private employers and recruiters, including defense contractors like Lockheed Martin, buying subscriptions on Dice and ClearanceJobs.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly by selling Dice and ClearanceJobs subscriptions; M&A is mentioned but acquisitions are occasional, not a steady roll-up.
mission_critical_reason: Recruiting job boards and subscriptions are easily switched; employers can use other job boards or LinkedIn with little disruption.
notes: Dice is the larger business; ClearanceJobs is the other part.

maintenance_led_reason: Mostly sells engineered components such as brake pads, Goulds pumps, valves and connectors to OEMs and industrial customers, mainly new equipment.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are mainly private automotive, industrial, chemical and energy companies; aerospace and defense is a smaller part.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly through its own engineered product lines in pumps, motion and connectors, with only occasional acquisitions.
mission_critical_reason: Components are qualified into customers' products and processes, such as auto brakes, pumps and aerospace connectors, so switching needs re-qualification.

maintenance_led_reason: Mostly sells chlor alkali, epoxy and ammunition as new products, not repair, servicing or replacement of installed equipment.
publicly_funded_reason: Chlor alkali, epoxy and Winchester ammunition are sold to industrial customers, distributors and consumers, not mainly government.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly through its chemical plants and Winchester ammunition operations, with only occasional acquisitions.
mission_critical_reason: Largest part is commodity chlor alkali and epoxy, which customers can buy elsewhere on price.
notes: Some specialty products, such as an insulin ingredient made only at Stade, are harder to switch away from, but they are a small part of the business.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue is recurring home medical supplies and equipment (diabetes, sleep, wound care, ostomy) for patients, not repair or maintenance of installed assets.
publicly_funded_reason: Apria and Byram bill Medicare, Medicaid and commercial insurers; the split isn't stated, so government share is unclear.
serial_acquirer_reason: Growth comes mainly from home-care products and services through Apria and Byram; Apria was a single large deal, not a steady roll-up.
mission_critical_reason: Patients depend on ongoing home respiratory, sleep, diabetes and ostomy supplies and equipment; switching disrupts care, insurer networks and prescriptions.
notes: Based on my recollection that Owens & Minor sold its Products & Healthcare Services segment, leaving home-based care; the payer mix is not confirmed.

maintenance_led_reason: Mostly SendTech installed base of postage meters and mailing systems: support services, supplies, rentals and financing, plus presort services.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are mainly private businesses, with some government and university clients such as the Missouri Department of Social Services.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows through its own mailing, shipping software and presort business; it is not an acquisition roll-up.
mission_critical_reason: Postage meters, mailroom systems and shipping software are embedded in operations and postal-compliant, so switching means retraining and disruption.
notes: Maintenance-led is a judgement call: revenue mixes equipment leasing, supplies and services, and the site gives no revenue split.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue is insurance brokerage commissions and fees on policy placement and renewals, not repair, servicing or replacement of installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are private businesses, individuals and employers buying insurance and benefits; commissions come from commercial and personal premiums.
serial_acquirer_reason: Insurance brokerage that has grown through steady acquisitions of middle-market brokers, including O'Leary in Ireland, as its core strategy.
mission_critical_reason: Clients can move brokers at renewal, though insurance advice matters; switching is moderately easy, so not strongly locked in.
notes: Mission-critical is a judgment call; brokers are sticky through relationships but clients can change brokers at renewal.

maintenance_led_reason: Sells canned and packaged fruits and vegetables, consumable food products, not repair or servicing of installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Revenue comes from retail, foodservice, and industrial customers, plus some government food programs, but mostly private buyers.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly through its own vertically integrated processing and sales of canned vegetables, with only occasional acquisitions.
mission_critical_reason: Canned fruits and vegetables are largely commodity or private-label food; retailers and foodservice buyers can switch suppliers easily.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue is management fees from managed REITs and private capital vehicles, not repair, servicing or replacement work.
publicly_funded_reason: Fees come from REITs, private investors and tenants-paid real estate vehicles, not government payers.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows by managing REITs and raising private capital funds and separate accounts, not by buying companies in a roll-up.
mission_critical_reason: Long-term external management contracts with affiliated REITs run their properties; switching manager is costly and disruptive.
notes: Mission-critical rests on long-term external management agreements with affiliated REITs; ease of switching is somewhat uncertain.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes mainly from manufacturing and selling new RVs (Airstream, Jayco, Heartland, Thor Motor Coach) to dealers, not repair or aftermarket.
publicly_funded_reason: New RVs are sold through dealers to consumers who pay privately for recreation; government is not the final payer.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grew via some large acquisitions (Jayco, Heartland, Erwin Hymer) but mainly grows by selling its RV brands; deals occasional.
mission_critical_reason: Dealers and consumers can switch among competing RV brands easily; discretionary recreational vehicles with no integration or regulatory lock-in.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes from software (Venue VDR, ActiveDisclosure, Arc Suite) and transaction-driven compliance filings, not repairing or replacing installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are private companies, investment funds, banks and law firms buying filing, data room and compliance software and services.
serial_acquirer_reason: Growth comes mainly from its own software and compliance products, such as Venue and ActiveDisclosure, with only occasional acquisitions.
mission_critical_reason: SEC filings, regulatory reporting (Arc Suite) and deal data rooms are compliance-critical, with workflow embedded and high switching risk.
notes: Part of revenue is transaction-driven (IPOs, M&A) and print/proxy services, which could vary; the answers reflect the larger software and compliance part.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue mainly from sample storage and management services, GENEWIZ genomics services and new cold-storage equipment/consumables, not servicing installed base.

serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly organically through sample management and multiomics services; acquisitions like UK Biocentre are occasional.
mission_critical_reason: Regulated cGMP storage of irreplaceable samples and drug products; switching risks chain-of-custody, compliance and sample integrity disruption.

maintenance_led_reason: Sells new closures, metal food cans and plastic containers as consumable packaging to consumer goods and food companies, not repair or aftermarket.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are private consumer goods and food companies buying closures, metal containers and custom plastic containers.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly through its own packaging business with periodic acquisitions; it is not a continuous roll-up.
mission_critical_reason: Food cans, dispensing closures and pharma/health containers are qualified into customers' products and filling lines, so switching is costly.
notes: Mission-critical is a judgment call; packaging is often multi-sourced, though qualification and line integration raise switching costs.

maintenance_led_reason: Sells Vafseo and Auryxia, prescription drugs for kidney disease; new prescriptions, not repair or servicing of installed equipment.
publicly_funded_reason: Auryxia and Vafseo are used mainly by dialysis and CKD patients, largely covered by Medicare and Medicaid.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows by developing and selling its own drugs; the Keryx deal was a single large acquisition.
mission_critical_reason: Prescribers can switch patients to alternative anemia or phosphate-binder drugs; the cost of switching is modest.
notes: Public funding share is inferred from the patient mix, not stated on the website text.

maintenance_led_reason: Sells consumable snacks and shakes (Atkins, Quest, OWYN) used up by consumers; not repair or maintenance of installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Revenue comes from consumers buying Quest, Atkins and OWYN products via grocery, club, mass and e-commerce retailers.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly through brand sales and new products; Atkins, Quest and OWYN were a few large deals, not a steady roll-up.
mission_critical_reason: Consumers and retailers can easily switch to competing snack bars, chips and shakes; commodity-like consumer packaged foods.

maintenance_led_reason: MRO distribution of bearings, pumps, safety and industrial supplies plus repair services for customers' existing operating facilities and equipment.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are private industrial firms in manufacturing, oil and gas, agriculture and construction, not government payers.
serial_acquirer_reason: Acquisitions are a significant part of growth history, but it mainly grows organically through distribution, service and supply chain sales.
mission_critical_reason: Mostly distributed MRO products from third-party brands, which customers can source elsewhere; some integrated supply and pump service stickiness.
notes: Serial-acquirer and switching-cost answers are judgment calls; DXP has made many acquisitions over time.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue is recurring payment processing fees and banking services on transaction volume, not repair, servicing or replacement of installed items.

serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly by adding merchants (about 3.7K per month) and products; acquisitions occur but aren't the main growth route.
mission_critical_reason: Embedded payment processing, MX Merchant POS, payables and banking-as-a-service are integrated into customers' operations, so switching means re-integration and disruption.
notes: Serial-acquirer answer is a judgment call; the company has made acquisitions historically, but the website emphasises organic merchant growth.

maintenance_led_reason: Builds, resurfaces and maintains roads, highways and runways; the site gives no split between new construction and maintenance work.

serial_acquirer_reason: Strategy is to acquire locally led infrastructure companies; recent Texas, Florida and Oklahoma acquisitions announced.
mission_critical_reason: Paving contracts are bid by public agencies and customers can switch contractors easily, despite owned asphalt plants and aggregates.
notes: The share of repair and maintenance versus new construction is not stated on the website.

maintenance_led_reason: Sells packaged food brands (Green Giant, Crisco, Ortega); consumables used up, not maintenance of installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Revenue comes from grocery retailers and consumers buying packaged foods, not government.
serial_acquirer_reason: Built its portfolio of 50+ brands by acquiring established food brands; website states commitment to acquiring brands.
mission_critical_reason: Shelf-stable grocery products; retailers and consumers can easily switch to competing brands.
notes: Acquisition pace has slowed recently as the company has focused on debt and divestitures, so the serial acquirer answer is somewhat uncertain.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes from dealer subscriptions for listings, advertising and digital marketing software, not repair or servicing of installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Paid by private auto dealers and manufacturer advertisers; consumers use the marketplace free.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly organically via its marketplace and dealer products, with only occasional acquisitions like Dealer Inspire and FUEL.
mission_critical_reason: Dealers can shift listing and advertising spend to rivals like CarGurus or Autotrader; marketplace is not core operating software.
notes: Dealer website and software products (Dealer Inspire) have some stickiness, but the larger marketplace/advertising part is easy to switch.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes from renting and selling DURA-BASE composite mats for new project site access, not repairing or servicing installed items.
publicly_funded_reason: Customers are mainly private utilities, pipeline and energy companies renting mats for projects, not government agencies.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly by renting and selling its own DURA-BASE mats; only a few small acquisitions like WGS, UAS, Lentzcaping.
mission_critical_reason: Temporary matting rentals for work pads and access roads can be switched to other mat suppliers fairly easily.
notes: Mat rental and sales is the larger business; a smaller environmental services business also exists.

maintenance_led_reason: Revenue comes from advertising, media, PR and marketing services for brands, not repair or maintenance of installed assets.
publicly_funded_reason: Clients are private brands and companies (consumer, healthcare, tech); advertising is paid by businesses, not government.
serial_acquirer_reason: Grows mainly organically through agency networks and client wins; the large IPG merger was one big deal, not a roll-up.
mission_critical_reason: Brands can review and switch advertising and media agencies, though data and media integration adds some friction.
notes: Switching difficulty is moderate; agency reviews happen regularly, so mission_critical is a judgement call.
